classification.difficultyReason: The units must be unified (cm and m) before finding a leg by subtraction. Rounding to the nearest centimetre follows.

content.prompt:
A tent pole 280 cm tall stands upright on level ground. A rope 3.4 m long runs from the top of the pole to a peg in the ground.
How far is the peg from the base of the pole to the nearest centimetre?

answer.worked:
Write both lengths in centimetres: $3.4\text{ m}=340\text{ cm}$. The rope is the hypotenuse.
$$\begin{align*}a^2+b^2&=h^2\\x^2+280^2&=340^2\\x^2&=340^2-280^2\\x^2&=37\,200\\x&=\sqrt{37\,200}\text{ cm}\\x&\approx193\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The peg is 193 cm from the base of the pole, to the nearest centimetre.
